title: Adrenal gland removal (adrenalectomy)
what: The surgeon removes an adrenal gland, a small gland on top of the kidney. Usually through a few small openings.
why: For an adrenal tumor, especially if it makes extra hormones and raises blood pressure.
duration: surgery usually takes 1 to 3 hours, with 2 to 5 days in hospital
tell_doctor: All your medicines, especially blood thinners. Your doctor will say what to stop and when
Allergies to medicines, latex, or iodine
Your blood pressure and all your blood pressure medicines
Episodes of racing heart, sweating, or headache

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: Blood tests, an ECG, and sometimes a GP checkup. The clinic will give you a list.

prepare.title: Hormones
prepare.text: Sometimes medicines are taken for a few weeks before surgery to prepare your blood pressure. An endocrinologist prescribes them.

prepare.title: Anesthetist
prepare.text: Before surgery, an anesthetist will talk with you. Tell them about your health and medicines.

prepare.title: Food and water
prepare.text: Usually no food from the night before and no drinks for a few hours. The clinic will tell you the exact time.

bring: CT scans and hormone test results
Your blood pressure diary, if you keep one
steps: You change, and an IV line is placed
The anesthetist gives anesthesia and watches your blood pressure
You are placed on your side or stomach
The surgeon removes the adrenal gland through small openings
feel: Pain in the side and at the openings. You will get painkillers
Blood pressure may change. It is checked often
after: You start getting up and walking early
Sometimes hormone tablets are needed for a while. Your doctor will prescribe them
Blood pressure and blood tests are checked after surgery
Lab results usually come in 1 to 2 weeks
red_flags: Severe weakness, dizziness, vomiting, or a drop in blood pressure: call emergency services
A fever over 38°C (100.4°F), or pus from the openings
Calf pain, shortness of breath, or chest pain: call emergency services

faq.a: Usually yes. The other one copes with the work.

faq.q: Will my blood pressure return to normal?
faq.a: It often improves, but not always right away. Your doctor will adjust treatment.

reminders.text: Surgery tomorrow. Take your medicines as your doctor planned. Eat and drink only until the time the clinic gave you.
